summary: EU, US, UK, Canadian and many other passports enter Ukraine visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period, and eligible others can use the official eVisa. The UK FCDO says Ukraine's airspace is closed and its borders with Belarus and Russia are closed; its advice covers the crossings with Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, Romania and Moldova.

conflict.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine — visa information
conflict.states: E-Visa applications are processed within 9 working days

alsoStatedOn.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine — Visa information (e-Visas: single or double entry 30-day visas)

applyWindow.text: Submit the application no later than 3 working days before the trip starts, or 1 working day for urgent processing.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine — e-Visa portal (home page)

processing.text: All e-Visa applications are processed within urgent (1 working day) or non-urgent (3 working days) procedure.

stayDays.text: E-Visas are issued to foreigners-holders of passports of 45 specified countries as single or double entry 30-day visas

fee.notes: Basic fee at Ukraine's embassies and consulates for regular service; doubled for expedited service. Some nationalities pay a different, reciprocal fee.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine — visa information

fee.text: Ukraine’s Embassies/Consulates abroad charge $65.00 (basic visa fee) for processing visa applications via regular service.

processing.text: in up to 10 working days from the day of application within regular service unless stipulated otherwise by Ukraine’s international treaties. Processing time of an application filed within regular service may be extended for up to 30 working days if additional checks are necessary.

stayDays.text: C type visas are issued in cases where a foreigner/stateless person intends to stay in Ukraine for up to 90 days within every 180 days.

validityDays.text: C type visas are issued as single / double / multiple entry visas valid for 6 months or another period depending on supporting documents

passportValidity.text: The UK FCDO tells British nationals travelling without a visa that their passport should be valid for the proposed stay, with no extra validity required. Canada's travel advice tells Canadians at least 6 months beyond the date they leave Ukraine. No Ukrainian source we could read states the rule.

source.name: UK FCDO — Ukraine travel advice: entry requirements

conflict.name: Government of Canada — Ukraine travel advice
conflict.states: passport valid at least 6 months beyond the date you expect to leave Ukraine

travelInsurance.text: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says e-Visa applicants upload a health insurance policy with EUR 30,000 of cover. The UK FCDO says permanent residents of Ukraine do not need to show proof of insurance; no official source we could read states the rule for visa-free visitors.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine — e-Visa (documents to upload: health insurance policy, EUR 30,000 coverage)

alsoStatedOn.name: UK FCDO — Ukraine travel advice: entry requirements

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read requires an onward ticket. Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 884 lists a return or onward ticket with a fixed date as one way to show sufficient funds.

source.name: Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine — Resolution No. 884 of 4 December 2013 (sufficient financial means)

proofOfFunds.text: Required by law (Article 21 of the Law on the Legal Status of Foreigners). Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 884 of 2013 sets the amount at 20 times Ukraine's monthly subsistence minimum per month of stay, worked out per day as (20 × the monthly minimum ÷ 30) × (days of stay + 5). It can be shown with cash, a bank card with a statement, an accommodation booking, a tour voucher, a host's guarantee letter or a return ticket, and can be checked when a visa is issued and at the border.

source.name: Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine — Procedure for confirming sufficient financial support of foreigners (Resolution No. 884 of 4 December 2013)
source.instrument: Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 884 of 4 December 2013, paras 3, 4 and 8; Law No. 3773-VI, Art. 21

currencyLimits.text: Canada's travel advice says cash of €10,000 or more (or the equivalent in other currencies) must be declared to customs when entering or leaving Ukraine, and undeclared amounts above that may be seized.

source.name: Government of Canada — Ukraine travel advice (money)

notes: Canada's travel advice says not to photograph military installations, mobile or temporary defence equipment or government buildings — including drones overhead, air defences and downed aircraft or missiles.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says Russia's invasion is ongoing, with frequent missile and drone attacks across the country; it advises against all travel to most of Ukraine and against all but essential travel to some western regions, and says to identify shelter locations in advance and take shelter immediately when an air alert is announced. Canada advises against all travel to Ukraine.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Ukraine travel advice

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says Ukraine's airspace remains closed; check the travel advice for every country you cross.
The UK Foreign Office says to identify shelter locations in advance of any air alert and to take shelter immediately when one is announced; several air raid alert apps exist, including "Air Alert".

The UK FCDO says martial law is in place and to expect more document checks, transport restrictions and curfews, and to carry your passport at all times. Canada's travel advice says to follow local authorities' instructions at all times, including air raid sirens, curfews and evacuation orders.

The UK Foreign Office says Ukrainian and dual-national men aged 23 to 60 are prohibited from leaving Ukraine, and that the authorities may treat you as Ukrainian — for example if you have a Ukrainian parent or were born in Ukraine.
The UK FCDO says your travel insurance could be invalidated if you travel against its advice. Canada's travel advice says to get insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Ukraine?
faq.answer: Citizens of the EU, US, UK, Canada and a list of other countries enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Nationals of the countries on the MFA's eVisa list can apply online for the official eVisa; others need a visa from a Ukrainian consulate. The UK FCDO says Ukraine's airspace remains closed.

faq.question: How do I get to Ukraine if there are no flights?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says Ukraine's airspace remains closed. Check the travel advice for each country you travel through.

faq.question: Is it safe to visit Ukraine right now?
faq.answer: No. The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to most of Ukraine, and against all but essential travel to some western regions. It says to identify shelter locations in advance of any air alert, and lists air raid alert apps such as "Air Alert".

faq.question: How does the Ukrainian eVisa work?
faq.answer: Eligible nationalities apply entirely online at evisa.mfa.gov.ua, uploading a passport scan, photo, insurance and supporting documents. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says applications are processed within 1 working day (urgent) or 3 working days; a single-entry eVisa costs USD 20 and allows a stay of up to 30 days.

faq.question: Do Ukraine's martial-law exit restrictions apply to foreign visitors?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says the exit ban applies to Ukrainian and dual-national men aged 23 to 60, and that if you also hold Ukrainian citizenship Ukraine may treat you as Ukrainian — for example if you have a Ukrainian parent or were born in Ukraine.

faq.question: Should I bring cash to Ukraine?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says credit cards are widely used in cities, but ATMs might not be refilled, some bank cards might not be accepted, and card terminals may not work during power cuts — and to make sure you have enough cash in local currency. Canada's travel advice says cash of €10,000 or more must be declared to customs when entering or leaving Ukraine.
